Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

- Diagram I shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219315/assets/aad13ab456bc61c90522725ddb60f481c6138a9e53a50136d691ddd344349cf1.png)

- Diagram II shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219315/assets/143e831321a485a0e57b706c6df89273bd92b3134d691d1ef41a67b7f7076481.png)

- Diagram III shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219315/assets/2c361eea2a598de063dc62375716ca5bdb7b0a06d4c30cf9a5c420cd9cc48e4b.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
html:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

  • Diagram I shows three points that are not collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.
  • Diagram II shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.
  • Diagram III shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
